baseline.name: Key-count table with min/max scan
baseline.approach: Update counts in a hash map and scan all keys for each extreme-count query.
baseline.time: Expected O(l) updates and O(k) min/max scan for k bounded-length keys

archived.name: Ordered count buckets plus key hash
archived.time: Expected O(l) inc/dec; worst O(k*l) hash search; O(1) min/max lookup
archived.space: O(H+k+b), H=100003 and b frequency buckets

why: Adjacent count buckets maintain the ordering incrementally so extreme queries read the first or last live bucket.
quantitative_comparison: A min/max query avoids scanning k keys and reads a bounded number of links. This benefit is conditional on successful state maintenance and bounded keys, not an elapsed speedup claim.
tradeoffs: Extra bucket/list complexity and a fixed key buffer replace simple scans. The archived destructor leaks remaining keys/interior buckets, and strcpy depends on the key-length constraint; overall implementation quality is not superior merely because queries are faster in the work model.
evidence_basis: Static query-cost comparison with known cleanup/bounds limitations explicitly retained; no benchmark.
